objective: Migrate all production SQL access to MyBatis Repository/Mapper layers while preserving API, authorization, tenant, transaction and audit behavior.

requirements.statement: All production SQL is owned by MyBatis Mapper/XML or Repository; Controller and Service contain no direct SQL access.
acceptance: static scan finds no direct SQL in Controller/Service
all SQL paths have Mapper/XML tests

requirements.statement: Each migrated module exposes Controller, Service and Repository/Mapper boundaries without changing public APIs.
acceptance: existing routes and DTOs remain compatible

requirements.statement: Module, integration and full feature tests prove behavior, permissions, transactions, audit and pagination remain equivalent.
acceptance: MySQL/Flyway and full Maven regressions pass

requirements.statement: Each module migration has an independent rollback point and no unresolved high-severity feedback.

invariants: tenant and entity authorization remain server-side
writes retain transaction and audit behavior

assumptions.text: Existing SQL can be represented by MyBatis XML or annotated Mapper with equivalent parameter binding
assumptions.basis: current project already contains MyBatis dependencies and Mapper/XML examples
assumptions.falsifier: unsupported vendor-specific SQL or result behavior

unknowns.question: Which modules contain dynamic SQL or implicit transaction coupling not covered by tests

decisions.decision: Use explicit Repository interfaces backed by MyBatis Mapper/XML and migrate modules serially
decisions.reason: preserve business boundaries and isolate rollback

measurement_intents.method: module boundary check and code review
